title: 2006 AMC 12A Problem 25
statement:
How many non-empty subsets \(S\) of \(\{1, 2, 3, \ldots, 15\}\) have the following two properties?

\((1)\) No two consecutive integers belong to \(S.\)

\((2)\) If \(S\) contains \(k\) elements, then \(S\) contains no number less than \(k.\)

solutions.text:
By property \((2),\) a valid \(k\)-element set is a \(k\)-subset of \(\{k, k+1, \ldots, 15\}\) with no two consecutive elements.

Collapsing the gaps between chosen elements, these correspond bijectively to \(k\)-subsets of a \((17 - 2k)\)-element set, counted by \(\binom{17 - 2k}{k}.\) This is nonzero only for \(k \le 5,\) so the total is \[ \begin{gathered} \binom{15}{1} + \binom{13}{2} \\ {}+ \binom{11}{3} + \binom{9}{4} \\ {}+ \binom{7}{5} \\ = 15 + 78 + 165 + 126 + 21 \\ = 405. \end{gathered} \]

Thus, the correct answer is E.
